# Moving Toward a Greener Future: 2025 Transit Awards

## Methodology and Supporting Analysis

## Data Acquisition

### Task 1a: State Electricity Profiles

```{r}
#| label: task-1a-electricity
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(tidyverse)
library(stringr)
library(httr2)
library(rvest)

get_eia_sep <- function(state, abbr){
    library(tidyverse)
    library(stringr)
    library(httr2)
    library(rvest)
    library(fs)
  
    state_formatted <- str_to_lower(state) |> str_replace_all("\\s", "")
    
    dir_name <- fs::path("data", "mp02")
    file_name <- fs::path(dir_name, state_formatted)
    
    fs::dir_create(dir_name, recurse=TRUE)
    
    if(!fs::file_exists(file_name)){
        BASE_URL <- "https://www.eia.gov"
        RESPONSE <- request(BASE_URL) |> 
          req_url_path("electricity", 
                       "state", 
                       state_formatted) |>
          req_headers(
            `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0"
            ) |>   
          req_retry(
                max_tries = 4, 
          ) |>
          req_perform(file_name)
    
        resp_check_status(RESPONSE)
    }
    
    TABLE <- read_html(file_name) |> 
        html_element("table") |> 
        html_table() |>
        mutate(Item = str_to_lower(Item))
    
    if("U.S. rank" %in% colnames(TABLE)){
        TABLE <- TABLE |> rename(Rank = `U.S. rank`)
    }
    
    CO2_MWh <- TABLE |> 
        filter(Item == "carbon dioxide (lbs/mwh)") |>
        pull(Value) |> 
        str_replace_all(",", "") |>
        as.numeric()
    
    PRIMARY <- TABLE |> 
        filter(Item == "primary energy source") |> 
        pull(Rank)
    
    RATE <- TABLE |>
        filter(Item == "average retail price (cents/kwh)") |>
        pull(Value) |>
        as.numeric()
    
    GENERATION_MWh <- TABLE |>
        filter(Item == "net generation (megawatthours)") |>
        pull(Value) |>
        str_replace_all(",", "") |>
        as.numeric()
    
    data.frame(CO2_MWh               = CO2_MWh, 
               primary_source        = PRIMARY,
               electricity_price_MWh = RATE * 10,
               generation_MWh        = GENERATION_MWh, 
               state                 = state, 
               abbreviation          = abbr
    )
}

EIA_SEP_REPORT <- map2(state.name, state.abb, get_eia_sep) |> list_rbind()
```

```{r}
#| label: verify-electricity-data

nrow(EIA_SEP_REPORT)
glimpse(EIA_SEP_REPORT)
summary(EIA_SEP_REPORT$CO2_MWh)
```
### Task 1b: Transit Energy Consumption

```{r}
#| label: task-1b-energy
#| message: false
#| warning: false

load_ntd_energy <- function(){
  library(readxl)
  library(httr2)
  library(tidyverse)
  library(fs)

  DATA_DIR <- fs::path("data", "mp02")
  fs::dir_create(DATA_DIR, recurse = TRUE)

  NTD_ENERGY_FILE <- fs::path(DATA_DIR, "2025_ntd_energy.xlsx")

  if(!fs::file_exists(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)){
    request("https://www.transit.dot.gov/") |>
      req_url_path(
        "sites",
        "fta.dot.gov",
        "files",
        "2026-09",
        "2025 Energy Consumption_260806.xlsx"
      ) |>
      req_headers(
        `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0"
      ) |>
      req_perform(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)
  }

  if(file.info(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)$size < 1e4){
    stop("Download failed. Delete the corrupted file and try again.")
  }

  to_numeric_fill_0 <- function(x){
    x <- if_else(x == "-", NA, x)
    replace_na(as.numeric(x), 0)
  }

  read_excel(NTD_ENERGY_FILE) |>
    select(-c(
      `Reporter Type`,
      `Reporting Module`,
      `Gallons of Other Fuel`,
      `Other Fuel Description`
    )) |>
    mutate(across(
      -c(`Agency Name`, `Mode`, `TOS`),
      to_numeric_fill_0
    )) |>
    group_by(`NTD ID`, `Mode`, `Agency Name`) |>
    summarize(
      across(where(is.numeric), sum),
      .groups = "keep"
    ) |>
    mutate(
      ENERGY = sum(c_across(where(is.numeric)))
    ) |>
    filter(ENERGY > 0) |>
    select(-ENERGY) |>
    ungroup()
}

NTD_ENERGY <- load_ntd_energy()
```
### Task 1c: Transit Service Provided

```{r}
#| label: task-1c-service
#| message: false
#| warning: false

load_ntd_service <- function(){
  library(httr2)
  library(tidyverse)
  library(fs)

  DATA_DIR <- fs::path("data", "mp02")
  fs::dir_create(DATA_DIR, recurse = TRUE)

  NTD_SERVICE_FILE <- fs::path(DATA_DIR, "2025_ntd_service.csv")

  if(!fs::file_exists(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)){
    request("https://data.transportation.gov/resource/4fir-qbim.csv") |>
      req_url_query(`$query` = paste(
        "SELECT `_5_digit_ntd_id` AS `NTD_ID`",
        "`max_agency` AS `AGENCY`",
        "`max_reporter_type` AS `reporter_type`",
        "`max_organization_type` AS `organization_type`",
        "`max_city` AS `city`",
        "`max_state` AS `state`",
        "`mode`",
        "`type_of_service`",
        "`max_primary_uza_code` as `uza_code`",
        "`max_primary_uza_name` as `uza_name`",
        "`max_primary_uza_area_sq_miles` as `uza_sq_miles`",
        "`max_primary_uza_population` as `uza_population`",
        "`max_service_area_sq_miles` as `service_area_sq_miles`",
        "`max_service_area_population` as `service_area_population`",
        "`questionable_record` as `flagged_likely_inaccurate`",
        "`sum_unlinked_passenger_trips_upt` as `total_upt`",
        "`sum_passenger_miles` WHERE caseless_one_of(`report_year`, '2025') limit 50000",
        sep = ","
      )) |>
      req_headers(
        `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0"
      ) |>
      req_perform(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)
  }

  if(file.info(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)$size < 1e4){
    stop("Download failed. Please check the cached service file.")
  }

  read_csv(NTD_SERVICE_FILE) |>
    mutate(
      flagged_likely_inaccurate = !is.na(flagged_likely_inaccurate)
    )
}

NTD_SERVICE <- load_ntd_service()
```

### Question 3: Average U.S. Electricity Emissions

```{r}

national_co2 <- EIA_SEP_REPORT |>
  filter(
    !is.na(CO2_MWh),
    !is.na(generation_MWh),
    generation_MWh > 0
  ) |>
  summarise(
    average_co2 = weighted.mean(
      CO2_MWh,
```

The generation-weighted national average is `r round(national_co2, 1)` pounds of CO2 per MWh.

### Task 3b: NTD Energy Usage

#### Question 6: Five Transit Agencies with the Highest Fuel Consumption

```{r}
#| label: task-3b-top-fuel-agencies
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(tidyverse)
library(gt)

# Combine fuel consumption across transit modes
agency_fuel <- NTD_ENERGY |>
  group_by(`NTD ID`, `Agency Name`) |>
  summarise(
    across(starts_with("Gallons of"), ~sum(.x, na.rm = TRUE)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Identify the five highest-consuming agencies
top_fuel_agencies <- agency_fuel |>
  mutate(
    total_gallons = rowSums(
      pick(starts_with("Gallons of")),
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  ) |>
  slice_max(total_gallons, n = 5, with_ties = FALSE)

# Prepare a breakdown of fuel types
fuel_breakdown <- top_fuel_agencies |>
  select(`Agency Name`, starts_with("Gallons of")) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("Gallons of"),
    names_to = "Fuel Type",
    values_to = "Gallons"
  ) |>
  filter(Gallons > 0) |>
  mutate(
    `Fuel Type` = str_remove(`Fuel Type`, "^Gallons of ")
  ) |>
  arrange(`Agency Name`, desc(Gallons))

fuel_breakdown |>
  gt(groupname_col = "Agency Name") |>
  cols_label(
    `Fuel Type` = "Fuel Type",
    Gallons = "Gallons Consumed"
  ) |>
  fmt_number(
    columns = Gallons,
    decimals = 0
  ) |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Five Transit Agencies with the Highest Fuel Consumption",
    subtitle = "Fuel consumption by type, 2025"
  ) |>
  tab_source_note(
    source_note = "Source: National Transit Database, 2025"
  )
```

## Data Integration

### Task 4: Joining Transit and Electricity Data

```{r}
#| label: task-4-join-data
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(dplyr)

# Standardize agency IDs in the energy data
energy_ready <- NTD_ENERGY |>
  mutate(NTD_ID = sprintf("%05d", as.integer(`NTD ID`))) |>
  rename(transit_mode = Mode) |>
  select(-`NTD ID`)

# Combine service records for each agency and mode
service_ready <- NTD_SERVICE |>
  group_by(NTD_ID, mode) |>
  summarise(
    state = first(na.omit(state), default = NA_character_),
    agency = first(na.omit(AGENCY), default = NA_character_),
    total_upt = sum(total_upt, na.rm = TRUE),
    passenger_miles = sum(sum_passenger_miles, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  rename(transit_mode = mode)

# Join energy and service data
transit_combined <- energy_ready |>
  left_join(
    service_ready,
    by = join_by(NTD_ID, transit_mode),
    relationship = "one-to-one"
  )

# Add state electricity emissions
transit_combined <- transit_combined |>
  left_join(
    EIA_SEP_REPORT |>
      select(abbreviation, CO2_MWh, primary_source),
    by = join_by(state == abbreviation),
    relationship = "many-to-one"
  )

# Check the combined dataset
cat("Energy records:", nrow(energy_ready), "\n")
cat("Joined records:", nrow(transit_combined), "\n")
cat("Missing states:", sum(is.na(transit_combined$state)), "\n")
cat("Missing emissions factors:",
    sum(is.na(transit_combined$CO2_MWh)), "\n")

glimpse(transit_combined)
```

### Task 5: Preparing Electricity Emissions Factors

```{r}
#| label: task-5-electricity-factors

library(dplyr)

# Add the 2024 EIA emissions factor for Washington, DC.
# Puerto Rico remains NA until a comparable factor is available.

transit_combined <- transit_combined |>
  mutate(
    CO2_MWh = if_else(
      state == "DC" & is.na(CO2_MWh),
      937,
      CO2_MWh
    ),
    electricity_factor_available = !is.na(CO2_MWh)
  )

# Check remaining unmatched records
transit_combined |>
  filter(!electricity_factor_available) |>
  count(state)

# Check records requiring an electricity factor
transit_combined |>
  filter(
    !electricity_factor_available,
    `Kilowatt hours of Electric Propulsion` +
      `Kilowatt hours of Electric Battery` > 0
  ) |>
  select(
    `Agency Name`,
    transit_mode,
    state,
    `Kilowatt hours of Electric Propulsion`,
    `Kilowatt hours of Electric Battery`
  )
```

### Task 5: Total CO2 Emissions by Agency and Mode

```{r}
#| label: task-5-total-emissions
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(dplyr)

# Conversion factors: pounds of CO2 per reported unit
# Conventional fuels: EIA
# Biodiesel, ethanol, LPG, LNG: EPA
# CNG: estimated using a gasoline gallon equivalent
# Hydrogen: direct CO2 only; production not included

kg_to_lb <- 2.20462262

diesel_factor <- 22.45
gasoline_factor <- 20.86
cng_factor <- 116.65 * 0.114
biodiesel_factor <- 9.45 * kg_to_lb
ethanol_factor <- 5.75 * kg_to_lb
lpg_factor <- 5.68 * kg_to_lb
lng_factor <- 4.50 * kg_to_lb
kerosene_factor <- 21.78
bunker_factor <- 24.78

# Calculate emissions for every agency-mode pair
transit_emissions <- transit_combined |>
  mutate(
    fuel_co2_lbs =
      `Gallons of Diesel Fuel` * diesel_factor +
      `Gallons of Gasoline` * gasoline_factor +
      `Gallons of Compressed Natural Gas` * cng_factor +
      `Gallons of Bio-Diesel` * biodiesel_factor +
      `Gallons of Ethanol` * ethanol_factor +
      `Gallons of Liquified Petroleum Gas` * lpg_factor +
      `Gallons of Liquified Nat Gas` * lng_factor +
      `Gallons of Kerosene` * kerosene_factor +
      `Gallons of Bunker Fuel` * bunker_factor,

    total_electric_kwh =
      `Kilowatt hours of Electric Propulsion` +
      `Kilowatt hours of Electric Battery`,

    electric_co2_lbs = case_when(
      total_electric_kwh == 0 ~ 0,
      !is.na(CO2_MWh) ~
        (total_electric_kwh / 1000) * CO2_MWh,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),

    total_co2_lbs = fuel_co2_lbs + electric_co2_lbs,

    total_co2_tons = total_co2_lbs / 2000
  )

# Check calculation results
transit_emissions |>
  summarise(
    total_records = n(),
    calculated_records = sum(!is.na(total_co2_lbs)),
    missing_emissions = sum(is.na(total_co2_lbs)),
    total_co2_tons = sum(total_co2_tons, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```
## Task 6: Transit Emissions Efficiency

```{r}
#| label: task-6-emissions-efficiency
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(dplyr)

# Calculate emissions per trip and passenger mile
transit_efficiency <- transit_emissions |>
  mutate(
    co2_per_trip = if_else(
      total_upt > 0,
      total_co2_lbs / total_upt,
      NA_real_
    ),
    co2_per_mile = if_else(
      passenger_miles > 0,
      total_co2_lbs / passenger_miles,
      NA_real_
    )
  )

# Combine all transit modes for each agency
agency_efficiency <- transit_efficiency |>
  group_by(NTD_ID, `Agency Name`, state) |>
  summarise(
    total_trips = sum(total_upt, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_passenger_miles = sum(passenger_miles, na.rm = TRUE),

    # Preserve missing emissions rather than
    # treating them as zero
    total_emissions_lbs = if (
      any(is.na(total_co2_lbs))
    ) NA_real_ else sum(total_co2_lbs),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    co2_per_trip = if_else(
      total_trips > 0,
      total_emissions_lbs / total_trips,
      NA_real_
    ),
    co2_per_mile = if_else(
      total_passenger_miles > 0,
      total_emissions_lbs / total_passenger_miles,
      NA_real_
    )
  )

# Check agency-level results
agency_efficiency |>
  summarise(
    total_agencies = n(),
    complete_agencies = sum(!is.na(total_emissions_lbs)),
    incomplete_agencies = sum(is.na(total_emissions_lbs)),
    agencies_with_trips = sum(total_trips > 0),
    agencies_with_miles = sum(total_passenger_miles > 0)
  )
```
## Task 7: Green Transit Awards

### Checking Potential Award Winners

```{r}
#| label: task-7-check-candidates
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(dplyr)

# Check the lowest-emissions agencies in greater detail
candidate_agencies <- agency_efficiency |>
  filter(
    `Agency Name` %in% c(
      "City of Seattle",
      "Anaheim Transportation Network",
      "Tri-County Metropolitan Transportation District of Oregon"
    )
  ) |>
  select(
    NTD_ID,
    `Agency Name`,
    state,
    total_trips,
    total_passenger_miles,
    total_emissions_lbs,
    co2_per_trip,
    co2_per_mile
  )

candidate_agencies

# Examine the service modes and energy consumption
# of the leading candidate
transit_emissions |>
  filter(`Agency Name` == "City of Seattle") |>
  select(
    transit_mode,
    total_upt,
    passenger_miles,
    fuel_co2_lbs,
    electric_co2_lbs,
    total_co2_lbs,
    total_electric_kwh
  )

# Check that candidate agencies have positive emissions
# and valid denominators
candidate_agencies |>
  summarise(
    invalid_emissions = sum(
      is.na(total_emissions_lbs) | total_emissions_lbs <= 0
    ),
    invalid_trips = sum(
      is.na(total_trips) | total_trips <= 0
    ),
    invalid_miles = sum(
      is.na(total_passenger_miles) | total_passenger_miles <= 0
    )
  )
```
### Calculating the Green Transit Award Rankings

```{r}
#| label: task-7-award-rankings
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(dplyr)

# Award 1: Greenest Transit Agency
# At least 100,000 annual passenger trips

greenest_ranking <- agency_efficiency |>
  filter(
    total_trips >= 100000,
    !is.na(co2_per_mile),
    co2_per_mile > 0
  ) |>
  arrange(co2_per_mile)

greenest_winner <- greenest_ranking |>
  slice_head(n = 1)

greenest_median <- median(
  greenest_ranking$co2_per_mile
)

# Award 2: High-Ridership Green Leader
# Original award: at least 10 million annual trips

high_ridership_ranking <- agency_efficiency |>
  filter(
    total_trips >= 10000000,
    !is.na(co2_per_trip),
    co2_per_trip > 0
  ) |>
  arrange(co2_per_trip)

high_ridership_winner <- high_ridership_ranking |>
  slice_head(n = 1)

high_ridership_median <- median(
  high_ridership_ranking$co2_per_trip
)

# Show the five best agencies for Award 1
greenest_ranking |>
  select(
    `Agency Name`,
    state,
    total_trips,
    co2_per_mile
  ) |>
  head(5)

# Show the five best agencies for Award 2
high_ridership_ranking |>
  select(
    `Agency Name`,
    state,
    total_trips,
    co2_per_trip
  ) |>
  head(5)

# Show median values for comparison
data.frame(
  award = c(
    "Greenest Transit Agency",
    "High-Ridership Green Leader"
  ),
  eligible_agencies = c(
    nrow(greenest_ranking),
    nrow(high_ridership_ranking)
  ),
  median_emissions = c(
    greenest_median,
    high_ridership_median
  )
)
```
## Press Release

The Green Transit Alliance is announcing its first Transit Efficiency Awards to recognize public transit agencies that move people while producing very little carbon pollution. Ridership alone doesn’t tell the full story, and neither do emissions alone. Looking at them together shows how much climate impact each rider is responsible for. This year’s winners, the City of Seattle’s monorail service and Oregon’s TriMet, stood out because their emissions per rider were a small fraction of what is typical for agencies like them.

### Award 1 — City of Seattle (Monorail)

The City of Seattle’s reported monorail service earned the award for the lowest estimated emissions per passenger mile among agencies reporting at least 100,000 trips. The monorail produced just 0.064 lbs of CO₂ per passenger mile. The median for the 484 eligible agencies was 1.107 lbs, so Seattle’s figure is about 94% lower, or roughly one-seventeenth of the typical agency. This result applies only to the monorail operation Seattle reported, not to the city’s wider transit network.

```{r}
#| label: task-8-greenest-award-plot
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5.5

library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(scales)

# Top five eligible agencies
greenest_plot_data <- greenest_ranking |>
  slice_head(n = 5) |>
  mutate(
    agency_label = case_when(
      `Agency Name` == "City of Seattle" ~
        "City of Seattle (Monorail)",
      `Agency Name` ==
        "Tri-County Metropolitan Transportation District of Oregon" ~
        "TriMet (Oregon)",
      `Agency Name` ==
        "San Francisco Bay Area Rapid Transit District" ~
        "BART (California)",
      TRUE ~ `Agency Name`
    ),
    winner = if_else(
      `Agency Name` == greenest_winner$`Agency Name`[1],
      "Award Winner",
      "Other Agency"
    )
  )

ggplot(
  greenest_plot_data,
  aes(
    x = co2_per_mile,
    y = reorder(agency_label, -co2_per_mile),
    fill = winner
  )
) +
  geom_col(width = 0.65) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("%.3f", co2_per_mile)),
    hjust = -0.15,
    size = 3.8
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Award Winner" = "#2E785D",
      "Other Agency" = "#8A9DA6"
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 0.19),
    breaks = seq(0, 0.18, 0.03)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Greenest Transit Agency Award",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Five lowest-emission agencies | ",
      "Eligible agency median: ",
      round(greenest_median, 3),
      " lbs CO2 per passenger mile"
    ),
    x = "Pounds of CO2 per passenger mile",
    y = NULL,
    fill = NULL,
    caption = paste(
      "Sources: NTD 2025; EIA State Electricity Profiles 2024.",
      "Minimum 100,000 annual trips.",
      "Estimated operational emissions."
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 8)
  )
```
### Award 2 — TriMet (Oregon)

The Tri-County Metropolitan Transportation District of Oregon (TriMet) earned the award for large agencies serving at least 10 million passenger trips a year. TriMet produced an estimated 0.413 lbs of CO₂ per passenger trip, while the median among the 74 eligible agencies was 3.267 lbs. Put simply, the average ride on a typical large agency produces about eight times as much carbon as a ride on TriMet. Doing that at this scale shows that a big, heavily used system can still be very efficient.

```{r}
#| label: task-8-high-ridership-plot
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5.5

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

high_ridership_plot_data <- high_ridership_ranking |>
  slice_head(n = 5) |>
  mutate(
    agency_label = case_when(
      `Agency Name` ==
        "Tri-County Metropolitan Transportation District of Oregon" ~
        "TriMet (Oregon)",
      `Agency Name` == "MTA New York City Transit" ~
        "MTA New York City Transit",
      `Agency Name` ==
        "Port Authority Trans-Hudson Corporation" ~
        "PATH (New York)",
      TRUE ~ `Agency Name`
    ),
    winner = if_else(
      row_number() == 1,
      "Award Winner",
      "Other Agency"
    )
  )

ggplot(
  high_ridership_plot_data,
  aes(
    x = co2_per_trip,
    y = reorder(agency_label, -co2_per_trip),
    fill = winner
  )
) +
  geom_col(width = 0.65) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("%.3f", co2_per_trip)),
    hjust = -0.15,
    size = 3.8
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Award Winner" = "#2E785D",
      "Other Agency" = "#8A9DA6"
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.18))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "High-Ridership Green Leader Award",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Agencies with at least 10 million annual trips | ",
      "Eligible median: ",
      round(high_ridership_median, 3),
      " lbs CO2 per trip"
    ),
    x = "Pounds of CO2 per passenger trip",
    y = NULL,
    fill = NULL,
    caption = paste(
      "Sources: NTD 2025; EIA State Electricity Profiles 2024.",
      "Estimated operational emissions."
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 8)
  )
```

### Closing and Limitations

These estimates combine 2025 National Transit Database (NTD) ridership and fuel data with 2024 U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) electricity data, using standard emissions conversion assumptions. One Puerto Rico agency was left out of the complete-emissions rankings because no electricity emissions factor was available for it. The figures should be read as careful estimates, not exact measurements.
